title: Chronograph: Route-Model Matrix — compact specs
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Design spec and prototype notes for a compact Route-Model matrix (aka 'Chronograph') that surfaces latency, throughput, token distribution and cost signals at a glance for per-route and per-model slices. This ticket covers the visual language, chart-level aggregation rules, interaction patterns (hover, scrub, compare), and rollout/annotation overlays needed for the Redwood Console. The primary goal is a dense, scannable grid that supports quick triage (SLO breaches, cost spikes, regressions) and deep-dive transitions into full-route views.
goals: Make per-route and per-model performance comparable in a single pane
Enable quick triage of latency P95/P99, median throughput, and token consumption per request
Surface cost-per-token and cost-per-request microcards for immediate economic signal
Support canary/rollout overlays and deploy annotations so changes correlate with metrics
Preserve readability at small sizes and meet color-contrast/accessibility standards
ux_constraints: Tiles must remain legible at 240x140px minimum
Visual density should not exceed 3 data layers per tile without explicit hover expand
Streaming/real-time data must gracefully degrade to 1m rollup on slow queries
Colors must meet WCAG AA contrast for critical alerts
layout_spec: Matrix grid: rows = routes (sortable), columns = model variants. Each cell is a compact tile with three microcharts and one microcard
Tile components: sparkline for 1m-6h token throughput, micro-waterfall for median->p99 latency bands, histogram for token-length distribution, and a small cost microcard
Top header: filter controls (time window, region, plan tier) + search by route/model + pinned route list
Right rail: quick legend, selected cell details (drill-in button) and rollout timeline summary
chart_specs: Throughput sparkline: line area, 60s sampling, window selectable (15m/1h/6h/24h), Y-axis autoscale with optional per-row normalization toggle
Latency micro-waterfall: stacked percentile bands (50/75/90/95/99) rendered as layered filled areas; tooltip shows exact percentile values at time cursor
Token-length histogram: 8 bucket log-scaled histogram showing request token distribution; overlay vertical lines for mean and 95th percentile
Cost microcard: computed cost-per-1000-tokens and cost-per-request over selected window, delta vs previous window and spark delta icon
Annotation layer: deploy events drawn as vertical lines; canary windows shaded with toggles to color by outcome (success / regression / neutral)
Alert overlay: SLO breaches flagged with red outline and context pill listing breached metrics (e.g., p99>750ms)
Sampling rules: default 100% up to 1k RPS, degrade to reservoir sampling above that; when sampling active, show sample rate badge
interactions: Hover a tile to reveal microtooltip with 3-line summary (p50/p95/p99, avg tokens, cost-rate)
Temporal scrub: hover horizontally to align all tiles to same timestamp for cross-model comparison
Click tile: open detail drawer anchored to tile with full-time-series, logs link, and quick actions (pin, annotate, create incident)
Multi-select: cmd/ctrl-click tiles to compare two or three variants side-by-side in comparison mode
Keyboard navigable grid with focus states and accessible labels for screen readers
prototype_notes: Figma prototype v1 created: link in attachments. Prototype includes hover micro-tooltips, scrub example and canary overlay simulation
Animation rules: sparklines animate on load but snapshots used for export to static docs to avoid test flakiness
Performance: minimal DOM layers; use canvas for sparkline rendering where many tiles are visible

notes_for_engineering: Provide endpoints that allow retrieving aligned timestamps across selected tiles for temporal scrub
Expose sample_rate and sample_source in the tile payload
Server should return percentile bands with consistent time buckets; client renders bands as area fills
Support deploy annotations with fields: timestamp, deploy_id, variant, outcome (success|regression|neutral)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: visual noise when many anomalies are present. Mitigation: thresholding and collapse option to show only top-3 signals per row
Risk: too many network requests for large matrices. Mitigation: batch tile requests and use a paginated viewport for offscreen tiles
Risk: sampling introduces analytic confusion. Mitigation: surface sample rate and link to raw logs for high-fidelity debugging
